The last-day extra race for the boats who did not qualify: the medal boats are absent from it, not scored DNC in it

ILCA 7 2026 — World Championship, Dun Laoghaire IRL · F3 · SI (reference-docs:events/ilca7-worlds-2026/SI-with-Amendment-2.md)

2 qualifying fleets · → Gold/Silver · discards: 1 discard from race 3. · medal race ×1
On the last day the 2026 ILCA 7 Worlds run two things at once:

  7.7  On the last day two Final series races are scheduled for the boats
       defined in SI 7.6. One additional Qualification series race is
       scheduled for the boats who did not qualify to the Final series.

That extra race is *not* the 2024 companion race scored from 11. It is an
ordinary Elimination series race, sailed by all three fleets, scored from 1
within each, discardable, and counting toward the discard ladder — which is
why the ladder in those SIs runs to twelve races. The Gold fleet sails it
ten boats short.

Here F2 is that race: b1 sails it for Gold while y1 and b2, who made the
medal fleet, do not. The point of the fixture is what their rows do NOT
contain — selecting the medal fleet does not delete a boat from her final
fleet, so without care she reads as a Gold boat who failed to start Gold's
last race and collects a DNC at the fleet's score base. She is simply
elsewhere, and has no F2 cell at all. (A boat who really did miss a final
race still gets an explicit DNC row from the scorer.)

Note what does not change: Gold's score base for F2 is still its assigned
size plus one — SI 18.5.2 counts boats assigned to the fleet, and all
three are still assigned to it.

Hand check, DNC base 4 throughout, one discard from 3 races, at most one
from the final series, and a lone final race protected:
  y1  Q 1,1  F1 1        -> F1 is the lone final race so far; discard Q1 = 2 -> halved 1
  b2  Q 2,1  F1 2        -> same, discard Q1                                 = 3 -> halved 2
  b1  Q 1,2  F1 3  F2 1  -> two final races now, so F1's 3 is discardable    = 4
then the medal race (base 3, x1): y1 1 -> 2;  b2 2 -> 4.
